chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Prepare food, be choosy in it, and invite your companions over it'.

key_terms.تَنَوَّقْ: be choosy / refine / show preference in quality

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for preparing and sharing food with friends?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that the physical preparation and refinement of food (*tanawwuf*) are acts of worship that facilitate social cohesion, provided they are accompanied by sincere invitation. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) in daily life, where sharing high-quality sustenance serves as a tangible means of strengthening bonds of brotherhood (*ukhuwwah*) and expressing gratitude to God. The instruction reflects the broader tradition of valuing the material aspects of life when infused with spiritual intention and communal generosity.
